E1.evidence: Issue #2265 (iron binaries, Cyclone, rclcpp_action) reports the feedback callback running after the user cancelled and dropped the goal handle, causing segfaults; the reporter published a reproducer ("I created an example that triggers the bug : https://github.com/jmachowinski/rclcppActionDeadlock branch callAfterDrop") with log lines such as "stateChangeFeedback for ID 29 called but handle was dropped ptr is 0x7f9a44002260". The fix PR #2281 ("fixes https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2265") was merged into rolling on 2024-04-15 (839348c60174049da974faecce1d83cc0b07ff90).

E2.evidence: The defect is a race inside rclcpp_action's own client logic between a user thread dropping the goal handle and the executor thread that has already locked the weak pointer and then invokes the callback: "The problem is not the lock itself, but the usage of weak pointers / shared pointers." ... "This thread has a internal copy of the shared pointer to the handle, and will call the callback." ... "Note, this race condition also appears in all other callbacks." (jmachowinski, https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2265#issuecomment-1685839599). It occurs with any correct action server and any application that drops the handle from another thread; PR #2281 states the library now "acts according to its documentation", i.e. the fault was the library not meeting its own documented lifetime guarantee. The fix is internal to rclcpp_action (recursive mutex, clearing result_callback_ after use) plus a new stop_callbacks() API.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated past E2. The race occurs while the client application and the executor thread are active concurrently (multithreaded executor).

E4.evidence: "This leads to segfaults for us, as we delete the objects associated with the ClientGoalHandle once its cancelled." and the reproducer log "stateChangeFeedback for ID 29 called with invalid handle ptr is 0x7f9a44002260".

ineligible_reason: internal: use-after-drop race inside rclcpp_action's Client (callbacks invoked through an internally held shared_ptr copy after the user dropped the goal handle), independent of any action server; fixed within rclcpp_action by PR #2281 (recursive mutex, result callback cleared after use, new Client::stop_callbacks()). The reporter's original expectation that feedback stops right after async_cancel_goal was questioned by maintainers as server-side behaviour ("i think server publishes the feedback until the cancel request has been accepted on server side.", fujitatomoya), and is not the defect that was fixed.
